request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an **Export claims (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to the existing people export. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

It downloads `claims-<sheet>.csv`:
- The header line is `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`.
- There is one line per claim. People come in list order, retired people included, and each person's claims run oldest first.
- Each value is built the same way the claim row builds it on screen:
  - An unopened claim has an empty number.
  - A due with no rate shows `n/a`.
  - A claim whose due-by date falls in no period has an empty period.
- Quoting and line endings are the same as the people export. A value containing a comma, quote or line break is wrapped in quotes with inner quotes doubled, and every line ends with a line feed.

The change is front-end only, in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`; no server or stored-data changes were needed. I also moved the people export's download code into a small `downloadCsv` helper so both buttons share it. The people export's output is unchanged.
